what: Eni is Italy's integrated energy company. It explores for and produces oil and gas, with a strong position in Africa and the eastern Mediterranean, refines and sells fuel in Italy, and has spun renewables and biofuels into separate listed vehicles.
customers: European utilities and industrial gas buyers, Italian motorists and fuel distributors, and chemicals customers.
money: oil and gas production, heavily weighted to Africa and the Mediterranean
gas sales and liquefied natural gas trading
Italian refineries, service stations and the Versalis chemicals arm
renewables, retail power and biofuels, both partly sold to outside investors
moat: Exploration success in North and West Africa with pipelines that run directly to Italy, giving Europe gas that does not travel by sea.
risks: Operations in Libya, Egypt, Nigeria and Mozambique carry political risk
Net margin of about 3% is thin even for an oil company
The chemicals business has lost money for years
Debt of about $44 billion against $25 billion of cash
opportunities: Selling stakes in Plenitude and Enilive raises cash and shows their value separately
African gas supplies Europe at a time when it is replacing Russian volumes
A dividend yield near 4.5% plus buybacks
watch: Upstream production in Africa and the sale of further stakes in the energy transition businesses.
